News.title: Britain set for glorious 36C highs next week as UK set for 5th heatwave – smashing 30-year record for sunny days
News.content:
BRITAIN is set for glorious 36C highs next week as the UK gears up for its fifth heatwave of the year.

The Met Office says temperatures will rise through the weekend as the hot spell builds across England and Wales, with yellow heat health alerts in force.



Forecasters add that temperatures could reach 30C on Saturday before climbing into the low 30s across southern and south-east England on Sunday.

The latest spell will be the fifth heatwave – an extended period of unusually hot weather for the time of year – to hit the country this year.



The hottest weather is expected on Thursday, when parts of East Anglia and the South East could hit a scorching 36C.

The Met Office says temperatures could reach around 30C across parts of England and Wales on Tuesday.



That could rise to between 32C and 34C on Wednesday before temperatures peak on Thursday.

And the sizzling spell could smash a 30-year record for the number of days Britain has reached 30C – temperatures have already reached 30C somewhere in the UK on 33 days this year.



The record stands at 34 days, set in 1995, and forecasters expect it to be broken next week.

Deputy chief forecaster Mike Silverstone said: “Temperatures will climb through the weekend and, more significantly, through much of next week.

“After a brief dip on Monday, high pressure will move across the UK before settling to the east, allowing a southerly flow to develop.

“A fairly widespread heatwave is likely across large parts of England and Wales, with hot conditions developing in places.

“The heat is expected to peak for much of England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Scotland on Wednesday, with up to 34C possible in parts of central and southern England and south-east Wales.



“East Anglia and south-east England, however, could see temperatures even higher on Thursday.

“Humidity levels are also expected to increase through the week, which may make conditions feel more uncomfortable, particularly overnight.”

Yellow heat health alerts have been issued for most of England until Tuesday.



They warn of possible impacts on health and social care services, as well as an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

The alerts are likely to be updated by the UK Health Security Agency in the coming days as the heatwave develops.

Temperatures will continue to rise as the weekend progresses, with the warmest weather expected in the south.

The UK has already seen some exceptionally hot weather this summer.

The year’s highest temperature so far was 38C, recorded at Lingwood in Norfolk on June 28.



The Met Office says there will be a clear split in the weather this weekend.

Scotland and Northern Ireland are likely to see some heavy rain, while England and Wales should stay largely dry and sunny.

But the long run of hot and dry weather has also left parts of Britain badly short of rain.

July was the driest month for England and Wales since records began in 1836, according to provisional Met Office figures.

Nineteen counties across England recorded just 1mm of rain or less throughout the whole of July.



Reservoir levels have also fallen, with storage in England now at 69 per cent.

That is down from 72 per cent a week earlier and almost 12 percentage points below the average for this time of year.

Five reservoirs have been classed as having exceptionally low levels.

They include Blagdon in Somerset, Hanningfield in Essex and Wimbleball in Somerset.

The dry weather has also increased the risk of wildfires, with conditions expected to be particularly severe across much of eastern and south-eastern England on Sunday.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Several major fires have already broken out across the UK in recent weeks, including blazes at Dunwich Heath in Suffolk and Headon Warren on the Isle of Wight.

The National Trust is urging people to sign a petition calling on the Government to make tackling climate change a national mission.

News.title: Migrant arrested after woman finds stranger lying next to her in just his PANTS after ‘breaking into her home’
News.content:
A MOROCCAN migrant has been arrested after allegedly breaking into a woman’s home and climbing into her bed in just his underwear.

Beatriz Ferron, 62, from Spanish enclave Ceuta, started screaming after waking up to find the near-naked intruder lying next to her.



Her cries alerted her husband and son, who had already got up for breakfast.

The suspect then fled the way he had entered, jumping onto the rooftop of an abandoned property next door where he was thought to have been sleeping rough.



The unnamed suspect, one of an estimated 70,000 migrants who stormed the Spanish enclave last month, was arrested nearby.

He was due in court today charged with breaking and entering, with officials expecting the case to be dealt with through a speedy trial.



The shocking incident emerged overnight as Beatriz spoke of her horror, while her son blasted politicians claiming life in Ceuta is returning to normal after the mass border breach.

The drama unfolded shortly before 8am yesterday at Beatriz’s fifth-floor apartment on Paseo de las Palmeras, or Palm Promenade, in central Ceuta.

Speaking to a local TV station after the arrest, the Spanish woman said: “It was a nightmare. This man has jumped over the balcony, got into my bedroom and got into my bed.

“I thought it was my husband, but when I turned over I discovered a stranger in his underpants in my bed.



“I started shouting and my husband who was having breakfast before going to work and my son who fortunately was also with us came running in.

“I hadn’t seen the intruder come in because I had my back turned to him. He fled the same way he came in.

“Thank God I wasn’t alone. Thankfully, the police responded very quickly and were able to arrest this man.



“Later today a speedy trial is due to take place, but I’m still in a state of shock.

“Someone who breaks into your house and gets into your bed into his underpants can’t have good intentions.

“I feel as if I’ve been attacked as a person and as a woman.”

Beatriz’s son Nacho described the extraordinary events in a social media post and thanked police for their swift response and arrest.

He then turned his anger on politicians, including Spain’s Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska.



He accused the minister, who has claimed the situation in Ceuta is back to normal after most of the irregular migrants left, of misleading the public.

He said: “Who do they want to deceive?

“This is not a feeling of insecurity. A stranger has entered my home and got into bed in his underpants next to my mum while she was sleeping. This is the reality.



“Today she’s been able to recount it. Who will be the next? How long will we have to put up with this?

“We have been abandoned and we need help.”

It comes as Ceuta braces for another surge of migrants to storm the enclave by speedboat.

Alicante-based tech company Golden Owl believes August 15 has been earmarked for the invasion.

It discovered mafia-run social networks offering places on a boat for around €14,000 (£12k).



The company also warned that August 10 is being considered as an alternative plan after the original date was leaked.

Sources from Spain’s National Intelligence Centre also confirmed the information, according to local media.

Golden Owl claims the new method will shift focus from swimming to the use of Zodiac boats.



The inflatables are often used by drug runners because they are powered by engines and capable of travelling at high speed.

The plan allegedly involves a “crowdfunding” offer stating: “Whoever has 15,000 dirhams (£12k) should come down to Fez.

“I’ll sell my motorcycle, and we’ll pool the funds to buy a Zodiac and use it to enter Ceuta. That way, they won’t send us back.”

Open recruitment on online forums is a deceptive tactic often used by criminal networks.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Golden Owl has linked 25 Facebook groups to the social media campaign that allegedly led to thousands of people joining the rush to reach Ceuta last week.



Spain’s Ministry of the Interior said it is prepared for a potential invasion.

News.title: Defiant Amanda Knox rants about ‘dry-humping’ & dismisses murder trial evidence as ‘just vibes’ in Fringe show debut
News.content:
AMANDA Knox ranted about “dry-humping” and dismissed murder trial evidence as “just vibes” in her controversial Edinburgh Fringe debut.

A defiant Knox took to the stage yesterday as she brazenly spoke about her false conviction for killing her flatmate Meredith Kercher in 2009.



She was greeted by cheers and whoops from a packed room in the Gilded Balloon, despite receiving fierce backlash from the tragic student’s family.

The 39-year-old lifted the lid on murder accusations, which she blamed on her simply being “a little too theatre kid”.



The performance came days after friends and family of Kercher slammed the show as “distasteful and disrespectful”, launching a petition calling for its cancellation that received more than 10,000 signatures.

But surrounded by children’s toys, Knox raged about her years being “vilified as a drug-addled succubus” and questioned how her notoriety will impact her own two children.



Knox returned to parts of her case that were held up as markers of guilt at the time, and dismissed them as “just vibes”.

Of her infamous kiss outside the crime scene in Italy, she said: “Even if I had been dry-humping his leg while making awkward eye contact with the lead detective, that would make me in heat, but it wouldn’t have made me a murderer.”



And on her Foxy Knoxy nickname, given to her by school friends and later picked up by the newspapers, she argued: “Even If my nickname were murder pussy, it wouldn’t make me a murderer.”

She added that the cartwheel she was alleged to have done while in police custody was in fact the splits – which is “a lot harder than a cartwheel”.

Knox addressed her tragic flatmate Meredith too, recounting stories of how the pair baked cookies together, shared clothes, and went thrift shopping together.



She said: “Meredith was so much more sensible than me,” adding that “after her murder, everyone was so intent on judging me.”

Clearly aware of her own divisiveness among the public, Knox compared herself to everything from “white-gold, blue-black dress”, to “a human version of haggis”.

But the audience at the opening night was clearly a supportive crowd, with more than half of the audience giving her a standing ovation at the end.



After the show Knox, who has written books and appeared in documentaries about her experience, greeted queues of fans to sign copies of her memoir – while cops patrolled the room.

She spent four years behind bars over her 21-year-old flatmate’s murder in 2007 before being cleared.

Her high-profile legal battles spanned nearly a decade until Italy‘s highest court overturned her conviction in 2015.



Leeds University exchange student Meredith, from Croydon, South London, was found dead in the flat in Perugia, Umbria, she shared with Knox, now 38.

Timeline of Meredith Kercher saga November 1, 2007 – The murder of Meredith Kercher: British exchange student Meredith Kercher, 21, is found dead in the apartment she shares with Amanda Knox in Perugia, Italy. Her throat is slashed, and signs suggest she may have been sexually assaulted. November 6, 2007 – Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito arrested: Amanda Knox, her Italian boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito, and Patrick Lumumba, Knox’s boss at a local bar, are arrested in connection with Kercher’s murder. Knox accuses Lumumba of the killing during a police interrogation. November 20, 2007 – Patrick Lumumba released: Lumumba is released after police find no forensic evidence linking him to the murder. He was falsely implicated by Knox during a contentious interrogation. December 6, 2007 – Rudy Guede arrested in Germany: Rudy Guede, a 20-year-old Ivorian man, is arrested in Germany and extradited to Italy. His DNA is found on Kercher’s body and at the crime scene. October 28, 2008 – Guede convicted of murder: Guede opts for a fast-track trial and is convicted of Kercher’s murder. He is sentenced to 30 years in prison, later reduced to 16 on appeal. January 16, 2009 – Knox and Sollecito trial begins: Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito stand trial for the murder of Kercher. Prosecutors allege a sex game gone wrong, while the defence argues that Guede acted alone. December 4, 2009 – Knox and Sollecito convicted: Knox and Sollecito are found guilty. Knox is sentenced to 26 years in prison; Sollecito receives 25 years. November 24, 2010 – Appeals process begins: Knox and Sollecito appeal their convictions. A key focus is the forensic evidence, including DNA found on a knife and a bra clasp. October 3, 2011 – Knox and Sollecito acquitted: An appeals court overturns their convictions, citing errors in the forensic investigation. Knox is freed and returns to Seattle. March 26, 2013 – Italy’s Supreme Court orders retrial: Italy’s Court of Cassation annuls the acquittals, ordering a retrial for Knox and Sollecito. January 30, 2014 – Knox and Sollecito reconvicted: Knox and Sollecito are reconvicted in their retrial. Knox, now in the U.S., is sentenced to 28.5 years in prison. March 25, 2015 – Final acquittal: Italy’s Supreme Court definitively acquits Knox and Sollecito of Kercher’s murder, citing lack of evidence and glaring errors in the investigation. November 2021 – Rudy Guede released: Rudy Guede, the sole person definitively convicted in connection with Kercher’s death, is released from prison after serving 13 years. 2023 – present – Knox’s slander conviction: Despite her acquittal, Knox is convicted of slander for falsely accusing Patrick Lumumba. 2023: The European Court of Human Rights rules that Knox’s rights were violated during her 2007 interrogation. June 2024: An Italian court upholds her slander conviction, a decision confirmed by Italy’s high court in January 2025.

She had been raped, beaten and had her throat slit.

Knox – an exchange student from the University of Washington – had known Meredith just under six weeks when the murder took place.

Knox and then-boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito were convicted of the 2007 killing and sexually assaulting Meredith in what was called a “sex game gone wrong”.

Their convictions were overturned and she received a definitive acquittal in 2015.



­Ivorian migrant Rudy Guede served 16 years for the crimes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Knox is now married to write Christopher Robinson with two children in the US.

Since her release from prison she has built a career as an author, criminal justice activist, media producer and stand-up comedian.

News.title: Married Afghan ‘killer turned his back on Christianity & acted like a single man’ before Brit found in suitcase
News.content:
THE married Afghan Christian convert accused of killing a Brit missionary reportedly turned his back on the religion before she was found dead.

Pro boxer Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, had also begun hanging around bars “as if he was a single man” in months before Elisabeth Ross’ body was found stuffed in a suitcase in central Athens.



Ahmadzai ditched his Islamic faith for Christianity after fleeing Afghanistan for Europe in 2016.

He would end up volunteering for the NGO that housed and fed him – EuroRelief – where he would meet Alaina, a wealthy and devout evangelical Christian, in 2018.



The couple tied the knot five years later and appeared to live a dream life in Athens, where they set up their own refugee charity called Love Every Nation.

But it all came crumbling down after they crossed paths with Scot aid worker Elisabeth, known as Lisa, whose body was found dumped in a derelict building on July 18.



Ahmadzai denies the killing, but admits transporting Lisa’s body in a suitcase, using her bank cards to withdraw thousands of euros, and stealing her phone to send messages that would mislead concerned loved ones.

The cracks in his marriage to Alaina had reportedly begun to show around 18 months before the shocking crime.

The American confided in two evangelical Christians from the southern US, saying she had noticed a change in her “very handsome” husband.

They told the Daily Mail: “There were problems going on in the marriage.



“She felt that he had started questioning his commitment to Christianity.

“He became more aloof and seemed more focused on boxing and his friends than doing “God’s work”, as Alaina put it.”

Alaina had also noticed that her husband was hanging around bars in Athens “as if he was a single man”.



They added: “She felt that he’d changed and wasn’t as passionate about Christianity as when they first met.”

Ahmadzai converted to Christianity within a year of arriving in Greece, but Alaina reportedly started questioning whether it was genuine or whether he had been trying to strengthen his refugee case.

Alaina’s friends believe that Lisa, who was a devout Christian herself, got caught up in the middle of the couple’s difficulties.

One theory is that Alaina may have confided in Lisa about her doubts, before the Brit confronted Ahmadzai and came under attack.

Ahmadzai had begun showing signs of disillusionment online.



Facebook posts dating back to last year see him accuse some Greek NGOs of exploiting refugees and volunteers for financial gain.

He claimed that they charged volunteers registration fees and wrote of crowded accommodation and misused donations.

Ahmadzai shared images promoting the slogan “Boycott corrupt NGOs”.



The Afghan was charged with homicide with intent, robbery and illegal gun possession and refused to enter a plea during a court hearing on Thursday.

Ahmadzai could now spend the next 18 months in a hellish prison with terrorists, rapists and some of Greece’s most hardened criminals.

Authorities are awaiting toxicological tests and analysis of vital organ tissue that will determine Elisabeth’s exact cause of death.

Alaina allegedly reported her husband to the cops after she became suspicious he was involved in Elisabeth’s death.



She told cops that she had met Elisabeth through volunteer work in Athens and had last seen her on July 12, after a Bible study meeting, according to Greek news outlet Protothema.

Days later, she heard reports of a body being found stuffed in a suitcase in an abandoned building in Athens.

Later that night, Alaina recalled waking up with a “terrible” feeling.

In the morning she then texted Elisabeth and got two replies which made her suspicious.



Alaina said: “These messages were not in Lisa’s style, both in terms of her level of English and the use of emojis that she never used.”

When she tried calling Elisabeth she didn’t get a reply.

Alaina also told police she had grown suspicious of her husband after she woke to find him missing on the evening of July 15.

When she checked his shared location, she saw he was in Elisabeth’s flat.



Having later confronted him, he told her he had been watching a football match but had gone to Elisabeth’s apartment to use the toilet.

She told police: “I don’t know what to tell you, but all of the above made me feel strange.

“Especially combining the dates, the messages and my husband’s behaviour, I have various thoughts that make me feel uncomfortable.”

Investigating officers also found CCTV footage which allegedly shows him leaving Elizabeth’s apartment with a suitcase and dropping it where her remains were discovered.



Ahmadzai has told cops he did not kill Elisabeth, saying he found her dead before panicking.

In his testimony, he reportedly said: “I never did harm to anyone. I want you to understand me and believe me. I was just in a panic.”

He is said to have claimed he had visited the house where she was staying and found her lying on the bathroom floor.

Ahmadzai claimed he panicked and fled and then encountered an elderly man near a bus stop and asked what he should do after finding a dead body.

He said he returned to the apartment the following day and placed Elisabeth’s body in a black suitcase, before placing it in the boot of the red Peugeot he drove.



“I found the old man I told you about who gave me the advice. He told me to leave the suitcase with him, and he would take care of it,” he reportedly said.

He admitted to the cops he had taken Elisabeth’s phone and bank cards.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Elisabeth’s devastated family paid tribute on Thursday – describing her as “kind, principled and selfless”.

They said: “Her integrity was absolute, and she dedicated her life to helping others in need. We are in deep pain, and we ask for time and privacy as we come to terms with our loss.”

News.title: Syrian refugee who posed as Good Samaritan to rape woman after tricking her into taxi on night out is jailed
News.content:
SINISTER ATTACK Syrian refugee who posed as Good Samaritan to rape woman after tricking her into taxi on night out is jailed

A SYRIAN refugee who posed as a “Good Samaritan” to rape a woman after tricking her into a taxi on a night out has been jailed.

Mohammed Al Masri, 25, offered to get the young mum home but instead took her back to his house where he carried out the vile sex attack, a court heard.



Al Masri and a second man followed the victim on her way home through Piccadilly Gardens, Manchester, on December 22 last year.

As she was on the phone to her boyfriend, Al Masri, who speaks Arabic and has limited English, approached the woman and pestered her with compliments.



When she became upset, he and his pal offered to get her an Uber home.

She saw them type in her address and believed them to be helping her.

But inside the cab she felt unsafe and shared her location with her boyfriend via Whatsapp, Minshull Street Crown Court heard.

The taxi driver later told police that the woman had passed out in the cab, and the two men had helped her out of the car.

She was taken into the bedroom of Al Masri’s Manchester house in Abbey Hey, where Al Masri raped her, while his friend remained in the room.

Officers arrested him soon after the attack after the young mum managed to send her live location to her boyfriend, who then alerted the police.



Cops located the address and found the woman in bed upstairs and arrested Al Masri at the scene in the early hours of December 22 last year.

Al Masri denied the offence and claimed sex was consensual, but was found guilty after a trial last month and sentenced to eight years in prison.

A 10-year sexual harm prevention order was put in place to prevent further offending.

Keith Harrison, defending Al Masri, said he was a “political refugee from the Assad regime” in Syria and that he was granted five years leave to remain, which expires in 2029.

He said Al Masri was not “work shy”, had no previous convictions, and described the offence as a “one-off”, reports the Manchester Evening News.



Judge Recorder Alexandra Simmonds said the victim was “in a vulnerable state”, “in no condition to make any free and informed decision about sexual activity”, and had to suffer the “degradation and humiliation” of the presence of a second man.

In a victim impact statement read in court, the woman said: “I will never forget the fear that I felt when this man took me to his house. I had no idea who he was.

“I had no idea where I was. I genuinely questioned if I would leave this place with my life.

“There were so many thoughts running through my mind when I arrived at his house however, this man tried to reassure me and tell me that I was going to be safe and my boyfriend was coming. This was all a sick lie.

“I remember not being able to move my body because I was so frozen with fear. I remember thinking ‘I am going to die.’



“I was thinking about my children and how they would be able to live without a mum. I just wanted it all to be over.

“The next thing I remember is the police entering the room and I have never felt relief like it. I knew I was going to live. This was not the end of what happened to me. I feel like this was only the beginning.

“I will never be able to forget what this man did to me. This man has changed me. When I met up with my friend on December 21, I was a different person then, to who I am now.”

The brave mum added: “After it all happened, I felt like I was a zombie. I could not speak to anybody. I was numb. I was emotionless. I felt nothing. I couldn’t interact with my children and felt like I was unable to be a real mum.”

Detective Constable Oliver Smith, of Greater Manchester Police, said: “I hope the sentencing of this vile sexual predator offers her a sense of solace while she looks to move on and rebuild her life.



“I urge anyone who might have experienced rape or sexual assault to please come forward and report it. You will always be listened to and supported.”

Anna Mackenzie, from the Crown Prosecution Service, said: “Mohammed Al Masri posed as a ‘good Samaritan’ when he offered to help the woman get a taxi home after a night out, but his motives were far more sinister.

“The way he targeted a lone woman who he believed would be vulnerable through alcohol was both calculating and insidious. Al Masri’s vile actions have had a lasting impact on the woman.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I truly hope today’s sentence will help her move forward, knowing that without her bravery and support this dangerous man would still be in our community.

“There is no place for rape or sexual violence in our society, and the CPS is determined to bring offenders to justice.”

News.title: Golf legend’s mansion next door to Royal Lodge on sale for £3.5million after Grand Designs-style refurbishment rejected
News.content:
IN THE ROUGH Golf legend’s mansion next door to Royal Lodge on sale for £3.5million after Grand Designs-style refurbishment rejected

GOLF legend Justin Rose’s six-bedroom mansion next door to Andrew Mountbatton-Windsor’s old Royal Lodge home, is on the market for £3.5million.

Documents seen by The Sun show the golfer, 46, and his wife Kate bought the sprawling Georgian property near the gates of the Windsor Park estate in September 2024.



The former gatehouse backs onto Windsor Great Park and forms part of the Crown Estate – near Andrew’s old home.

Rose’s links to his former neighbour, known as Randy Andy, stretch back decades to when he was an aspiring golfer.



In 1998, when Rose was one of Britain’s brightest golf prospects, Rose played a round at Sunningdale with Andrew alongside fellow young golfer Rebecca Hudson.

The future Ryder Cup star later met the then prince again when the he launched the Duke of York Champions’ Trophy, an event aimed at helping the country’s most promising juvenile golfers.

TV and radio star Chris Evans previously rented The Gate House for around two years, reportedly paying a whopping £6,000 a month.

In 2019, Evans was stopped by Andrew’s security after trying to drive through Windsor Great Park in his 1964 Aston Martin DB5.



The presenter had attempted to take a shortcut through the Crown Estate entrance in the vintage car, which is worth around £1.2million.

The route would have saved him both time and miles on a journey to a property he was renovating in Ascot, just days after Andrew stepped back from royal duties.

In April this year, just days after a heart-breaking near-miss at the Masters in Augusta, golfing icon Rose lost a planning battle over proposals to extend the Grade II-listed home in a Grand Designs-style refurbishment.

The Ryder Cup star had wanted to demolish part of the 19th-century property to build an “orangery”.

Plans also included a new ground-floor kitchen and breakfast room, bar, family area and master bedroom with a secure closet and office.



But the local council rejected the application, saying the proposed two-storey extension would be “excessively prominent, awkward, overly large” and would harm the historic building.



Rose, who is from Hampshire and has two children, appealed the decision.

But a Government planning inspector has now upheld the council’s ruling after visiting the property.

Documents show the mansion has now been put up for sale with a £3.5million asking price – £150,000 more than he bought it for.

The Rose family also own a multi-million-pound home on Surrey’s exclusive Wentworth Estate.

Andrew was forced out of Royal Lodge last year after his brother King Charles stripped him of his prince title and dukedom.



The 31-room mansion and six cottages in the estate’s grounds have since been left looking like a ghost town.

Andrew, 66, handed back his 75-year lease on Royal Lodge to the Crown Estate amid the fallout from the Jeffrey Epstein scandal last year but did not leave until February.

He has since moved into Marsh Farm on the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, with the property funded by the King.

Andrew’s peppercorn-rent deal had previously meant daughters Beatrice and Eugenie were expected to inherit the £30million mansion.

Claims Queen Camilla could inherit the property if Charles dies before her have been widely dismissed.



Prince William and Princess Kate are also not interested in moving in after securing a 20-year lease on nearby Forest Lodge.

Andrew, who was once the UK’s trade envoy, was arrested at Marsh Farm on February 19 – his birthday – by Thames Valley Police on suspicion of misconduct in public office.

Detectives then searched both his Sandringham home and his former Windsor residence, Royal Lodge.

Police have been investigating claims Andrew leaked Government information to his paedophile financier associate Jeffrey Epstein, who died in a New York jail in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges.

Andrew has denied any wrongdoing.



The investigation is continuing, with detectives now expected to travel to the US to speak to the family of his accuser Virginia Giuffre.

Giuffre, who took her own life last year aged 41, received a multi-million-pound payout from Andrew in an out-of-court settlement in 2022. He did not admit any liability.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Andrew was stripped of his royal titles last year.

The Sun has approached Justin Rose for comment.

News.title: Daring mission to retrieve Mount Everest ‘Green Boots’ climber after 30 years as mystery identity finally cracked
News.content:
A DANGEROUS operation is set to bring home Everest’s most infamous frozen body after the chilling mystery was finally solved after 30 years.

Known as “Green Boots” because of the distinctive lime-green footwear still protruding from the ice, the dead mountaineer has become one of the world’s most haunting landmarks.



Authorities believe the body belongs to Dorje Morup, an Indian climber who died in a savage blizzard while descending Mount Everest in 1996.

His remains have been frozen in the mountain’s deadly “death zone” ever since – more than 26,000ft above sea level.



But after three decades of mystery, a high-altitude rescue team is now being sought to attempt the perilous mission of bringing him down.

Dorje’s identity was finally established through evidence including his clothing and climbing equipment.



Authorities now hope DNA testing can provide definitive confirmation.

The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), which is funding the operation, wants his remains returned by September.

For Dorje’s family, it could finally end an agonising wait that has lasted three decades.

His wife, Konchak Yangskit, never fully accepted that her husband was dead.



She told the BBC: “On some days, before I went to sleep, I would think that there’d be a knock on the door tonight and that when I opened, he would be there.

“When he comes home, I will ask him: ‘Where were you all these years?’”

Dorje had left home in Ladakh in 1996 with a heroic promise.

He told his wife he would return from Everest as a hero and make his country proud.



Konchak told the BBC: “He asked me to take care of the kids and come to the airport to greet him on his return.

“I wondered if I was ever going to see him again.”

Dorje was a 48-year-old lance naik, or lance corporal, in the ITBP and an experienced Himalayan trekker.

He was one of six climbers attempting to make history by reaching Everest’s summit from the treacherous Chinese side.



Three members of the expedition turned back when a savage snowstorm swept across the mountain.

Dorje continued towards the 8,849m summit with fellow climbers Tsewang Smanla and Tsewang Paljor.

The trio eventually radioed their team leader at around 3.45pm Nepal time, reporting that they had reached the summit.

Poor visibility may have made it impossible to establish exactly where they were.

Howling winds ripped across Everest, temperatures plunged and visibility collapsed.



From below, members of the expedition spotted two headlamps moving above the Second Step at around 28,000ft.

It was the last time the three men were seen alive.

Dorje’s body lies in Everest’s notorious “death zone”, where temperatures can plunge to -40C and oxygen levels are around a third of those at sea level.

The Tibetan side of the mountain is particularly treacherous, with steeper terrain and fewer rescue facilities than the southern route.

The ITBP is now looking for a specialist mountain rescue group capable of taking on the dangerous mission.



If successful, his remains will be taken back to India for DNA testing – and if the tests confirm his identity, his family will finally be able to bury him.

“The weather and snow conditions are going to be crucial,” said Tshiring Jangbu Sherpa, a prominent Nepalese mountaineer who has taken part in other recovery missions.

“The north side has fewer crevasses, but it is riskier. If something bad happens from the Nepalese side, you get quickly evacuated by helicopter. But there is no such system from the Chinese side,” he told BBC Hindi.

Sherpa sources told BBC News Nepali that the lack of support on the Chinese side makes the recovery even more daunting.

Mountaineering guide Pemba Ongchu Sherpa said bringing the body down would be brutally difficult even in the more favourable spring season.



“It’s really tough to get that body down even in popular spring season, let alone the autumn [which has more unpredictable weather]. That’s the simple reason it is still there for so many years,” he said.

“There would need to be 10 to 12 climbers who are capable of making summits, just to fix [support] ropes to reach that point.”

The frozen remains would then have to be physically hauled down the mountain to an altitude where they could be collected by helicopter or possibly transported by yaks.

Bodies trapped in iced-up climbing gear can weigh several times the average man and become brutally difficult to move across Everest’s unforgiving terrain.

The remains can also begin to defrost and decompose once they reach lower altitudes.



Indian climber Kuntal Joisher warned the first stage of the descent could be the most dangerous of all.

“It’s going to be very, very risky endeavour. It’s extremely steep ground with lots of rock. Logistically, this [first] 1000m is going to be a humungous challenge.

“The main thing is to not put Sherpa lives at risk for a dead body.”

Experts say even relatively straightforward recoveries can cost between $40,000 and $80,000.

Recovering bodies from Everest has become more common over the past decade, but many of the hundreds who have died on the mountain remain where they fell.



Testimony from surviving members of the expedition, the location of the climbers’ final radio contact and Dorje’s clothing and equipment eventually led authorities to his identity.

An ITBP official, speaking anonymously, told BBC News Hindi that new evidence helped identify Dorje in recent years.

“We never forgot him. It was only a matter of time,” the official said.

For years, the family had only medals, trophies and a handful of photographs from Dorje’s mountain adventures to remember him by.

They also kept a certificate from the Chinese government stating that at 17:30 on May 10, 1996, Dorje reached the summit of Everest.



His son Punchok Dorjai says that if his father is finally brought home, the family will hold a funeral near Martyrs Park in Ladakh’s capital Leh.

“My father gave his life for the country and he should be remembered as a martyr,” Dorje said.

He said Dorje’s teammates who died alongside him deserve the same honour.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And the family already knows what they will do with one extraordinary reminder of the man who became an Everest mystery.

“We are planning to keep the Green Boots.”

News.title: Detective sacked for calling trans women ‘c**ks in frocks’ blasts decision insisting she’s ‘protecting female rights’
News.content:
A POLICE officer who was sacked after she opposed a policy which could have required her to strip search biological males says she has become a ‘scapegoat’ for speaking out about women’s rights.

Rachel Fletcher, a former detective constable, was horrified by new guidance which enabled officers and some detainees to self identify as men or women.



The framework meant that female officers could be required to conduct intimate searches of trans women who didn’t have a gender recognition certificate and hadn’t undergone reassignment surgery.

It also enabled biological male officers, identifying as women, to remove the clothing of female detainees when looking for forbidden objects.



The National Police Chief’s Council (NPCC) guidance, in place between 2022 and early 2024, was later suspended after criticism from politicians and amid legal concerns.

But last week Fletcher, who says she was an outspoken advocate for women’s rights and openly challenged the strip search policy, was hauled before a panel at Houghton Police Station near Sunderland.



The former detective, who worked in Northumbria Police’s Child Protection team, was told comments she had made about men and trans women amounted to “hatred”, and her behaviour was ruled gross misconduct.

Fletcher was accused of using the phrase “c***s in frocks” while discussing the controversial strip search policy with colleagues, an allegation she denies.



It was also claimed that Fletcher, who worked on an array of harrowing abuse cases, commented “all men are rapists” and “no wonder a f***ing man did it”, while talking about a crime.

Speaking after her sacking, the 49-year-old said: “I have been made a scapegoat.

“This isn’t about throwaway comments I might or might not have made.

“This has happened because I dared to speak out about the rights of women and girls.

“The strip search policy at the time was unlawful, and I dared to have an opinion on it. That’s my only crime.



“It was the most egregious, anti-dignity and unlawful guidance you could come up with and I don’t know how it got through.

“It was dangerous and irresponsible.

“No female officer should ever be in that position.”



After the Supreme Court’s ruling in April 2025, the NPCC issued new interim guidance making biological sex the default for intimate and strip searches.

The earlier policy enabling officers and some detainees to self identify was developed under the NPCC’s LGBTQ+ portfolio, led by Vanessa Jardine, the current chief constable of Northumbria Police.

It read: “Chief Officers are advised to recognise the status of Transgender colleagues from the moment they transition, considered to be, the point at which they present in the gender with which they identify.”

It added: “Thus, once a Transgender colleague has transitioned, they will search persons of the same gender as their own lived gender.”

In relation to detainees it reads: “All searches are dealt with on a case by case basis after consideration by a custody sergeant based on the response of the detainee.”



The guidance became highly controversial as it changed the policy of same sex searches to those based on gender identity.

In February 2024, it was criticised by the then Policing Minister Chris Philp who said: “It is not right, safe or respectful to detainees of either sex for officers to conduct searches on the basis of gender self-identification.”

Fletcher was a highly respected officer who recently led the investigation into the crimes of 39-year-old paedophile Ross Jackson.

He was later found guilty of 24 separate sexual offences and was jailed for 23 years at Newcastle Crown Court in February.

After she was sacked, Rachel’s supporters set up a GoFundMe page, which has so far raised £21,549 to help her and her children while she finds a new job.



She said: “If you’re in the police you’re not allowed to talk about misogyny or to call out gender ideology.

“I’ve been shut down for standing up for women’s rights.

“One of the comments I made was something along the lines of, imagine you are a female student officer and you are asked to carry out a strip search of a person you’ve been told is a woman, only to find they have a co**.

“How would she feel? Would she have the confidence to object?

“The crude language I used is commonplace in the office I worked in, where we spent every day describing the mechanics of sexual offences.



“It’s really difficult and horrible to be in this position but it’s the only way we are going to change things.

“If cops aren’t willing to stand up and sacrifice to do the right thing then who will?”

Fletcher was told she was being referred to the Professional Standards Department (PSD) on January 9 2024 after allegedly making the comments between February and December 2023.

She was put on limited duties after that, which meant she had no contact with the public.

On February 14 of the same year she was served with papers, informing her case would be going before a panel, chaired by Assistant Chief Constable Andy Hill.



Then, last week, it was ruled comments she was alleged to have made amounted to gross misconduct and she was sacked.

It was found Fletcher had breached the Standards of Professional Behaviour in relation to discreditable conduct, authority, respect and courtesy and equality and diversity.

She added: “I am absolutely devastated to have lost the job I loved.

“My dream was always to be a detective.

“At times my work was harrowing and really emotionally exhausting, but so rewarding.



“It was a real privilege.

“Policing is still very male dominated and it always has been.

“I think my sacking will have a negative impact on my colleagues. They will be terrified to speak up or challenge anything in case they are also dismissed.

“If I could have my job back, I would in a heartbeat because it’s such important work, I loved it.

“I don’t know what I’m going to do next – but I’ll keep going.



“It’s lovely to have this support and just incredible.

“People who have donated have given me peace of mind that I don’t have to worry about paying the mortgage or feeding my kids.”

During the hearing she admitted she said, “the only way to stop night time rapes is to put a 9 o’clock curfew on all men”, or words to that effect.

However, the former detective, who had worked at the force for 23-years, insists she was joking.

But the panel ruled Fletcher had made all the comments and dismissed her.



A spokesperson for Northumbria Police said: “The allegations faced were as follows:

“Between February and December 2023 and whilst on duty, the officer made comments about or in relation to men in general that were sexist, inappropriate and offensive.

“In or around January 2024, whilst on duty, the officer made a comment about transgender women in general which was transphobic, inappropriate and/or offensive.

“The panel found gross misconduct was proven in relation to both allegations and the officer was dismissed without notice.”

The National Police Chiefs’ Council (NPCC) was also contacted for comment.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It emphasised that new guidance was issued last May which makes clear police searches “such as those which expose intimate body parts, should be carried out by police officers and staff of the same biological sex as the detained person”.

However, it adds that “there may be very limited exceptions considered where someone requests to be searched by an officer of their gender”.

News.title: Man jailed after spending three weeks in hotel without paying - his final bill was massive
News.content:
Man jailed after spending three weeks in hotel without paying - his final bill was massive

A hotel stay that appeared to be an ordinary festive break has ended with a costly legal consequence for one guest after an unexpected discovery

View 3 Images The 54-year-old was sentenced to one year behind bars (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A man has been jailed after his hotel stay, that stretched through Christmas and into the New Year, ended with an unpaid bill running into thousands of euros.

‌



The guest had been staying at an accommodation in Spain when he eventually left without settling what he owed. The circumstances surrounding the stay have now resulted in a court ruling against him.

‌



The 54-year-old was sentenced to one year behind bars by the Provincial Court of Castellón after being found guilty of aggravated fraud, according to Diario De Sevilla. The case concerned his stay at Hotel L'Ermita Casa Ripo in La Vall d'Alba, near the Hermitage of San Cristóbal.

‌



He arrived at the hotel on December 22, 2023, and stayed on a full-board basis before leaving on January 15, 2024. During his time there, he received accommodation, meals and cleaning services.

The total cost came to €2,283.40.

According to the judicial ruling, the man secured the stay by "projecting an appearance of solvency" despite being "aware from the outset that he would not pay for any of the expenses incurred."

‌



View 3 Images The court imposed a €1,080 fine (Image: Getty Images)

The court found that his conduct amounted to aggravated fraud, with his previous criminal record playing a significant role in the decision.

The man had five previous final convictions for fraud offences. They included convictions handed down by courts in Barcelona, Salamanca, Tortosa and Santiago de Compostela between 2018 and 2024.

‌



The offences were considered particularly significant because they were of the same nature as the latest case. The court determined that his repeated offending demonstrated a pattern in which he gave the impression he had the means to pay before obtaining services without settling the resulting bills.

Proceedings eventually concluded on June 11, 2026, when an indictment reflecting an agreement between the defendant and his defence counsel was presented. He admitted the facts and accepted the sentence.

View 3 Images The man had five previous final convictions for fraud offences. (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Alongside the year-long prison term, the court imposed a €1,080 fine, payable at a rate of €6 per day over six months.

The ruling also states that failure to pay the fine could result in one day of deprivation of liberty for every two unpaid instalments.

The defendant has additionally been ordered to compensate Sociedad L'Ermita Casa Ripo S.L., the company behind the hotel, for the €2,283.40 outstanding from his stay. Statutory interest will also be added to the sum, while he has been ordered to cover the legal costs.

Article continues below

The ruling, numbered 244/2026, was handed down by the First Section of the Provincial Court of Castellón. It is now final and cannot be appealed by either party.

News.title: US accused of meddling in British politics with £370k of 'Trump Maga money' for education programmes'
News.content:
US accused of meddling in British politics with £370k of 'Trump Maga money' for education programmes'

A MP has accused the US government of 'meddling in our democracy' with a grant aiming to celebrate a Magna Carta memorial and topics including 'limited government' & 'taxation by consent'

View 4 Images An MP has accused the US government of using 'Trump's Maga money to meddle in our democracy' (Image: AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

The US government has been accused of attempting to "meddle in British democracy" with "Trump’s Maga money" through an educational grant.

‌



The US embassy in London opened an application, aimed at charities and NGOs, for a grant of up to $500,000 (£370,000) for a scheme labelled "Liberty Under Law: The Shared Anglo-American Tradition". This grant is intended to commemorate the 70th anniversary of a Magna Carta Memorial in Runnymede, Surrey, but criticism has been drawn to the wording used by the US government.

‌



The funding proposal appeared to use language aligned closely to the pro-Donald Trump Make America Great Again movement. For example one of the goals of the scheme was to reinforce "shared civilizational values".

‌



View 4 Images People visiting the Magna Carta memorial in Runnymede, in April 2025 (Image: Maureen McLean/REX/Shutterstock)

This scheme added that "priority will be given to ambitious initiatives that connect foundational principles" which included "limited government", "freedom of speech" and "taxation by consent".

‌



The Magna Carta Memorial in Surrey was erected in 1957 by the American Bar Association (ABA) - an organisation of US lawyers and law students. The ABA is not involved with this grant scheme from the US government.

A summary of the grant listing said: "The U.S. Department of State invites eligible organizations to submit proposals for innovative, high-visibility public education and civic-engagement programs in the United Kingdom that deepen public understanding of the shared Anglo-American common law tradition, and/or to commemorate the 70th anniversary in 2017 of the American Bar Association's unveiling of the Manga Carta Memorial in Runnymede, UK that honors the foundation of the rule of law."

View 4 Images View of the US embassy in London (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

‌



The proposal however says this grant will not support "projects relating to partisan political activity" or "lobbying for specific legislation of programs".

Despite this, the scheme and language used have been slammed by Liberal Democrat MP Lisa Smart who, according to the Guardian, said: "Magna Carta aimed to limit the powers of tyrants and said everyone was subject to the rule of law, something for which Trump has repeatedly shown utter contempt.

View 4 Images Liberal Democrat MP Lisa Smart has criticised the grant (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

‌



"We have a proud tradition of liberty and freedom of speech in this country and we don’t need Trump’s Maga money meddling in our democracy."

A recently departed US state department official, according to the Guardian, shared their concerns and said it was "highly unusual" to "specifically fund topics related to a narrow vision of America First is highly unusual".

This source reportedly accused the current US regime of attempting to "create UK-originated narratives to support Maga propaganda".

Article continues below

A spokesperson for the US embassy in London responded to the MP's accusation of "meddling" and said it was "mindful of such concerns, and has discontinued Biden-era public diplomacy spending on divisive ideological projects such as 'climate justice,' LGBTQ activism, and race-based hiring initiatives".

The Mirror has reached out to the US embassy in London for comment.

News.title: Royal Mail advice to people sending letters who include a county in the address
News.content:
Royal Mail advice to people sending letters who include a county in the address

Royal Mail has guidance for customers who like to include a county name in the address when sending a letter or parcel

View 2 Images A Royal Mail postbox - you might want to check their guidance before you next send a letter (Image: anouchka via Getty Images)

Royal Mail customers who like to include as much detail as possible on their addresses should check the postal service's guidelines first. Many people routinely add a full address when sending a letter or parcel.

‌



However, most people are unaware of the official guidance. According to the Royal Mail website, when posting a letter or item to someone in the UK, the address should include the recipient's name, the house number and street name, a locality name (if required), a town and the full postcode.

‌



It's worth noting that the town and postcode should be written in capital letters. Royal Mail states: "You don't need to write the name of the county if you've included the town and postcode."

‌



It also advises against using full stops and commas. It also recommends that senders align each line to the left rather than centring the text.

To ensure your post can be returned to you if necessary, Royal Mail also recommends including your UK return address on every item you send.

View 2 Images (Image: Jenny Matthews via Getty Images)

‌



But why does it matter whether you include the county name? Royal Mail's 2024 guide for clear addressing sets out exactly what people need to do when sending letters and other items.

It outlines what an address should contain. Back in 2010, Royal Mail announced that county names were to be removed from its postal database, known as the Postcode Address File, which lists every address in the UK and is widely used by businesses and public bodies.

People were told they could still include counties on addresses when posting letters, but were advised it was not necessary, as a house number, street and postcode are all that is required. Ian Beesley, chairman of the board that advised Royal Mail at the time on running the database, told the BBC back then that county names had become "a kind of vanity attachment".

‌



Royal Mail's guidance currently advises that the name of the recipient should be written or printed on the first line, above the address, with both their first name and surname included. A separate line can be added for an organisation name.

A line should then be used for the property number and street name. If the property has a full name, this can occupy one line, with the street name dropping down to the next.

The name of the local area or village can then follow on the next line, with the town name written in capital letters beneath that. Royal Mail notes: "You don't need to include a county name, as your letters and parcels will still reach the right place. However, you can include it if you prefer."

Article continues below

For UK destinations, the final line should be the postcode, also written in capital letters.

News.title: 'Good things are happening in Burnham’s Britain - families are being given breathing space’
News.content:
'Good things are happening in Burnham’s Britain - families are being given breathing space’

'As a Mancunian who spent some of my childhood growing up just yards away from Strangways prison, I’m delighted the new PM has opened a Downing Street office in Manchester’

View 3 Images Andy Burnham outside No10 for the first time as Prime Minister last month (Image: Dinendra Haria/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

Good things are happening in Burnham’s Britain.

‌



Within hours of taking office new Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his top team went into action unveiling new measures to help build a better Britain and start the hard work of delivering prosperity in every postcode.

‌



To give overstretched families the breathing space people have been crying out for VAT has been slashed from energy bills and bus fare caps.

‌



As a Mancunian who spent some of my childhood growing up just yards away from Strangways prison, I’m delighted the new PM has opened a Downing Street office in Manchester. We won’t fix the problems in the country unless every corner of the UK has a fair share and this radical new approach is about ensuring that finally happens.

Louise Haigh – who has already cemented her place in Labour history by renationalising the railways - is taking a chainsaw to the red tape and bureaucracy which too often block British businesses from winning government contracts. The government spends a whopping £90 billion a year on goods and services. That’s money which should be supporting British jobs. Louise Haigh’s new plan will guarantee exactly that.

New Chancellor John Healey will in the Autumn bring forward a budget to invest in Britain’s creaking infrastructure while Welfare Chief Pat McFadden and Education Secretary Lucy Powell have confirmed new training and skills proposals are in the pipeline to help get the million jobless youngsters into decent, well-paid work.

‌



View 3 Images Forme Labour Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary, Jonathan Ashworth (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

This all adds up to real meaningful action to build a sound and prosperous economy in every postcode. Labour values are at the heart of everything the government is doing.

On the international stage there is a welcome approach too with Ed Miliband as Foreign Secretary making climate change and international development guiding missions.

‌



Andy Burnham has apologised for Labour's stance on Gaza in the early days. Back in 2023, I wanted to publicly call for a ceasefire but instead Labour MPs were ordered to abstain when asked to support one in the Commons. That was the wrong call. Andy Burnham is right to acknowledge the previous Labour leadership got it so badly wrong.

On social care Andy Burnham has big radical plans too. When one in three born today will develop dementia in their lifetimes, fixing social care is an urgent challenge that can no longer be ducked. Anyone who has battled to secure care for a loved one suffering from dementia knows the current system is bust.

Labour created the national health service, now with Andy Burnham Labour will create the care service the country needs.

‌



Mental ill health can impact anyone

As a Labour MP I championed better mental health services and pushed to ensure mental health was taken as seriously as physical health.

Mental ill health can impact anyone and there is no shame in seeking help. This is very personal for me because my late dad struggled with drink addiction all his life and as someone recovering from a stroke, I know how stroke can lead to depression.

View 3 Images 'I’m so delighted to see Health Secretary Yvette Cooper making a big commitment to role out mental health community centres' (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



I’m so delighted to see Health Secretary Yvette Cooper making a big commitment to role out mental health community centres. Anyone will be able to help and support with addiction, finding work and financial problems.

This is the joined up thinking I was campaigning for. Building on the record numbers of children now getting quality mental health care and the recruitment of 8,500 extra mental health workers in the NHS, this government is delivering a transformation of mental health services.

Article continues below

Time for a Minister for Comedy?

Culture Chief Lisa Nandy says that when it comes to art, music, film and TV, Britain is brilliant. She’s right. In my old constituency, the arts scene thrives. But I was upset to learn the local Comedy Festival has gone bust. We all love a good laugh. I know plenty of politicians are comedians, maybe it's time for a Minister for Comedy to keep the nation laughing? Though on second thoughts…

Perils of Zoom calls

The video of a New Zealand politician joining a zoom call from her bathroom reminded me of the pandemic. I was doing constant zoom interviews from my kitchen. On one occasion my young daughters Grace and Annie zoom bombed me on live TV. To this day it's till the most successful interview I ever did.

News.title: Major update in hunt for child rapist who escaped while on escorted leave in Perth
News.content:
Major update in hunt for child rapist who escaped while on escorted leave in Perth

Cliff Lyons Dobbie absconded on Friday with a major manhunt launched

View Image Cliff Lyons Dobbie (Image: Police Scotland/PA Wire)

A convicted child rapist has been caught after he absconded from staff while on leave.

A major manhunt was launched for Cliff Lyons Dobbie on Friday after the restricted patient absconded from Perth, Scotland, while on escorted leave.

The incident sparked a widespread manhunt, with Police Scotland confirming Dobbie was caught on Saturday morning.

Dobbie was convicted of raping a 10-year-old girl in Glasgow while on bail for sexually abusing a 12-year-old boy in 1990. He was detained in secure units ever since, including psychiatric hospital, State Hospital Carstairs.

Police Scotland Tayside said in an update this morning: "We are pleased to confirm Cliff Lyons Dobbie has been traced.

Article continues below

"Thanks to everyone who shared our appeal."

News.title: Helen Flanagan laughs off taking only one kid on holiday after passport expiry blunder
News.content:
Helen Flanagan laughs off taking only one kid on holiday after passport expiry blunder

The mum of three has jetted off to Lake Como to celebrate her 36th birthday.

View 12 Images Helen was going to take Matilda but couldn't because of the passport drama (Image: @hjgflanagan/Instagram)

Corrie star Helen Flanagan has come under fire after joking about taking just one of her three children on holiday following a passport mishap. The actress, 36, had been planning a trip to Lake Como with her eldest daughter Matilda, 11, but discovered shortly before they were due to travel that the youngster's passport needed renewing.

‌



Helen previously revealed she had desperately tried to secure an emergency passport for Matilda but was unable to get one in time, leaving her daughter in tears.

‌



However, the actress has revealed the holiday is still going ahead – with her eight-year-old daughter Delilah joining her instead.

‌



12 View 12 Images Helen shared a lighthearted video of her and Delilah celebrating (Image: Instagram/ @hjgflanagan) 12 View 12 Images The pair joked that the other kids didn't have their passports (Image: Instagram/ @hjgflanagan)

Taking to social media, Helen shared a playful video of herself and Delilah having a drink at the airport as they celebrated being able to jet away together.

The mum-of-three, who also shares five-year-old Charlie with ex-fiancé Scott Sinclair, wrote over the clip: "When your brother and sister's passport is out of date but yours isn't."

‌



Helen could be seen laughing with her daughter in the video while dressed in a black crop top with her hair still in curlers ahead of their flight.

12 View 12 Images Helen has been sharing highlights from her trip (Image: Instagram/ @hjgflanagan) 12 View 12 Images Helen and Delilah look like they're having a great time (Image: Instagram/ @hjgflanagan)

‌



However, the light-hearted post didn't go down well with everyone, with some followers questioning why Helen had decided to continue with the holiday after Matilda's disappointment.

One person wrote: "Imagine being so selfish that you abandon two-thirds of your kids to go on holiday, and then make a jokey post about it....."

Another asked: "Why didn’t you put the holiday on hold until ya got the other two passports sorted out?"

‌



12 View 12 Images Helen is sunning herself on holiday in Italy (Image: Instagram/ @hjgflanagan) 12 View 12 Images The star is on holiday to celebrate her birthday (Image: Instagram/ @hjgflanagan)

While a third commented: "Sorry I hope you have a lovely trip but I don't think I could take my other daughter if the other had missed out through no fault of their own."

‌



The criticism comes after Helen shared her heartbreak over failing to get Matilda's passport sorted in time for the trip.

She explained earlier this week: "So I went down to Scotland, I fly to Lake Como on Thursday, to try to get Matilda an emergency passport and we've not been able to get one."

12 View 12 Images Last year, Helen and Matilda had a trip to Lake Como and the pair had been looking forward to going again (Image: @hjgflanagan/Instagram) 12 View 12 Images Helen revealed that Matilda had been in tears over the incident because she had been 'so looking forward' to the trip (Image: @hjgflanagan/Instagram)

‌



Turning to her upset daughter, Helen added: "I just thought I'd try it because it says a week, but you never know.

"Mummy tried her best, didn't she? Mummy has tried. Love you."

She later revealed just how disappointed Matilda had been, writing: "My little girls cried on my shoulder, she was so looking forward to our trip."

‌



The pair had enjoyed a mother-and-daughter holiday to Lake Como last year, with Helen previously speaking about enjoying the opportunity to spend quality time alone with her eldest.

12 View 12 Images The mum wanted to take her eldest daughter away (Image: @hjgflanagan/Instagram) 12 View 12 Images Helen tried to get Matilda's passport sorted (Image: @hjgflanagan/Instagram)

‌



While adults can potentially obtain replacement passports through the Passport Office's one-day premium service, the option isn't available for children under 16.

The quickest option for a child's new or replacement passport is instead the one-week Fast Track service, which requires an appointment and is subject to availability.

Helen shares all three of her children with former footballer Scott, whom she split from in 2022 after 13 years together.

‌



View 12 Images Helen starred as Rosie Webster in Corrie for years (Image: ITV)

The soap star has recently spoken about her hopes for her own romantic future, admitting she believes her next serious relationship could lead to marriage.

Speaking on Lewis Nicholls' Life Stories podcast, Helen said: "My next relationship I have I think will be my husband, because I won’t be wasting my time, really."

Article continues below

She also vowed to keep any future romance more private, explaining that she would want to "protect" the relationship from outside scrutiny.
