“It was a big ask in terms of coming back from America on Monday and you’ve got to give the lads credit for going close. There were a lot of positives in the performance.”

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho in December last year.

Scotland Yard said the striker had been charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm. Toney, who plays for the Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, is due to appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported in December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt. It claimed a fan recognised the footballer and grabbed at him while seeking a photograph with him before the incident.

On Friday the Metropolitan police said the charges related to an incident on 6 December at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London, reportedly the now-closed 100 Wardour Street.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was at the centre of one of the most curious transfers on deadline day in August 2024 when he completed a late move from Brentford to Al-Ahli worth a reported £40m. He has also played for Newcastle United and his home town club Northampton Town, as well as several others on loan as he looked to establish himself.

Seen as a late bloomer in football terms, he had made only two Premier League appearances before his 25th birthday, but went on to score 67 goals in 128 appearances over the next three seasons at the top level.

He has played 10 times for England, scoring once in a friendly match against Belgium in 2024, and was part of the 2026 World Cup squad, making appearances against Argentina in the semi-final and in the win over France as England finished third.

Sports.title: Jay-Z’s Roc Nation Sports making waves in European football transfer market
Sports.content:
In the end there was a clear winner. And Jay-Z’s latest victory came only 24 hours after the first record featuring him actually rapping for four years had been released by his wife, Beyoncé, on an extended remix pack of Morning Dew (Donk).

These days, the man who remains one of the most influential artists in hip-hop has his fingers in many pies, from the streaming service Tidal and his own streetwear brand, to champagne and cognac. But it is Roc Nation Sports – an offshoot of his entertainment company of the same name founded in 2008 – making headlines in the summer transfer window.

Established five years later in partnership with Creative Artists Agency, it began mainly representing players from the NBA, NFL and MLB, including Kevin Durant. Bayern Munich’s Jérôme Boateng was the first football client, in 2015, before Roc Nation Sports International (RNSI) was established four years later with a focus on stars at big European clubs.

Based in London, it now has more than 100 players on its books, including Vinícius Júnior – the Brazil forward who signed a lucrative new contract with Real Madrid this week believed to be worth around €25m. That came after Arsenal had been linked with a blockbuster move for the 26-year-old.

In July 2023 RNSI took over the successful Brazilian agents TFM – who already represented Vinícius, Gabriel Martinelli, and Endrick – and renamed it Roc Nation Sports Brazil.

In negotiations that have lasted two years, it had hoped to persuade Real to increase their star asset’s salary to €30m a year to match Kylian Mbappé, and allowed his contract to enter its final 12 months in an effort to drum up interest elsewhere. While Arsenal – now exploring other attacking options including Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye – are believed to have been willing to pay a big fee for Vinícius, it is understood that they thought signing him on a free transfer next season was more likely.

Nonetheless, Real upped their offer and Vinícius stayed. It is a decision that looks likely to cost them the chance to sign Rodri from Manchester City after Barcelona stole a march on their great rivals.

View image in fullscreen A phonecall from Vinícius Júnior reportedly led to Yan Diomande signing with Roc Nation Sports. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP

On the same day as the new six-year contract for Vinícius was announced, Yan Diomande flew to the Spanish capital to complete his record £115m transfer from RB Leipzig. The 19-year-old – who has made only 46 appearances at senior level for the German club and for Leganés in the Spanish second division but is already the most expensive African player in history – was pictured with his agents, Nathan Campbell and Kareem Gbaja on a private jet. RNSI has been reported to have been paid up to £17m in commission and fees.

A long-running saga that began when Liverpool had a £70m bid rejected by Leipzig in June ended with Diomande signing a seven-year deal at the Bernabéu on Thursday. It has provided a telling insight into the mechanisms of a modern transfer, with every week bringing a fresh twist. Having been told they must pay in excess of £100m to sign Diomande, Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the race at the end of July after releasing a statement that said the European champions “will not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents”.

RNSI has also had to fend off two legal challenges, including one from the former Bournemouth winger Max Gradel who claims that his agency, Maxidel Management, had an existing agreement with Diomande. Gradel has filed a complaint with Fifa, although world football’s governing body did not block the player’s move to Real. Dez Bamba – who is president of Diomande’s first club, AFI Sud Comoé in Côte d’Ivoire – has said that the winger was persuaded to join RNSI after receiving a call from Vinícius. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Meanwhile, the Rainbow World Group instigated proceedings at the high court in London and the British Virgin Islands against Diomande in mid-June “to enforce binding image rights and intellectual property agreements tied to his early career development”. It is claimed Rainbow invested significant resources in the winger, including taking him for trials at Chelsea, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Newcastle before he was signed by Leganés. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Given Diomande’s meteoric rise, perhaps it is no surprise that clubs are flocking to invest in African academies.

Jeff Luhnow – the former general manager of the Astros and St Louis Cardinals who won three World Series baseball titles and was chief executive of Blue Crow, the ex-owner of Leganes, until the club was sold to 885 capital in June - told the Guardian last year Diomande was expected to be the first of many after they set up recruitment and development programmes in several African countries, including Ghana and Zambia, in the past several years. “We’ve got more players like that in our pipeline,” said Luhnow.

RNSI announced in November that it has signed eight young African stars, including the Ghana Under-17 midfielder Joseph Narbi and Francis Gomez, a Gambian winger currently at AC Horsens in Denmark. “We believe Africa is a hotbed of untapped footballing potential, and our expansion here is a natural progression of our global vision,” said Campbell.

In the dog-eat-dog world of football agents Jay Z’s new kids on the block are certainly making their presence felt.

Sports.title: Manchester City reject Barcelona’s opening £38.5m bid for Rodri as talks continue
Sports.content:
Manchester City have rejected an offer of £38.5m (€45m) from Barcelona for Rodri and want at least £60m before allowing Spain’s World Cup-winning captain to depart.

Barcelona have emerged as Rodri’s preferred destination after talks with Real Madrid broke down this week. It is understood that the 30-year-old, who is now in the final year of his contract at City, has agreed personal terms with the Spanish champions after indicating that he would like to return to his homeland following the departure of Pep Guardiola.

Rodri moved to the Etihad in 2019 from Atlético Madrid and has turned down the offer of a lucrative extension. Yet City are believed to be adamant that he will not be allowed to leave for less than their asking price. Barcelona are continuing negotiations in the hope of reaching a compromise.

Rodri, who won the World Cup Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player last month, spoke to Barça’s manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, about a potential move on Wednesday.

The Spanish champions will be without Frenkie de Jong for several months after the Netherlands midfielder sustained a knee injury and have targeted Rodri as a replacement. He has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme.

City have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in negotiations with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi. The Morocco midfielder could cost up to £80m but they could be tempted to bring in a more experienced replacement for Rodri should he depart, with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández among those thought to be under consideration. The 25-year-old is also wanted by Real, whose manager, José Mourinho is said to not to have the news of being gazumped by their great rivals well. Reports in Spain have claimed that the 63-year-old is unhappy after making the signing of a central midfielder his priority on returning for a second stint at the Santiago Bernabéu.

Real have already brought in the winger Yan Diomande for £115m and Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Carlos Espí, so they may have to balance the books by selling either Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga if they want to pursue Argentinian Fernández.

Crystal Palace have confirmed the signing of Takehiro Tomiyasu after a successful trial period. The former Arsenal defender has been training with Palace during pre-season and has done enough to earn an initial 12-month deal with the option of extending that by another two years. Tomiyasu becomes new manager Pierre Sage’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Óscar Mingueza on a free transfer. Palace are expected to complete a deal for the USA youth international Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake in MLS.

Sports.title: Tracking private jets, Andrea Berta holding his nerve and a last-ditch plea from Matthias Jaissle: This is how Bruno Guimaraes became an Arsenal player - and why Mikel Arteta was so desperate to get him
Sports.content:
Tracking private jets, Andrea Berta holding his nerve and a last-ditch plea from Matthias Jaissle: This is how Bruno Guimaraes became an Arsenal player - and why Mikel Arteta was so desperate to get him

Unlock more from Isaan Khan inside the Arsenal camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

The back-and-forth over whether Arsenal and Newcastle are actually in talks, the plane trackings and the staunch denials in the North East are finally at an end.

Bruno Guimaraes is an Arsenal player, theirs for £75million, and a transfer saga which has dragged on for weeks, much to the entertainment of rival fans, is over. Mikel Arteta has his man, a player he’s long admired and been desperate to sign.

This transfer has been an exhausting process, and far from straightforward. But Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has come out of it looking incredibly shrewd, having pulled off a relative ‘bargain’ in the current climate.

Guimaraes' long journey to Arsenal started back in June. As Daily Mail Sport reported on June 24, the Brazilian had instructed agents to find him a new club and Newcastle were braced for an offer from the Gunners. Their interest had been registered.

Newcastle’s response was bullish. He wasn’t going anywhere, according to sources at the club. Given his status as captain and the player’s quality, Guimaraes’ value was enormous – particularly in light of the departures of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. They did not need to sell.

Money talks, however. Newcastle had briefed that they wanted closer to £100million, but internally there was acceptance that an offer of around £75million would see progress.

Bruno Guimaraes has joined Arsenal in a protracted £75million move from Newcastle

The transfer saga is finally over, with Guimaraes' long journey to Arsenal starting back in June

A force of nature.



Guimaraes is a Gunner ✍️ pic.twitter.com/E7k4mIHICg — Arsenal (@Arsenal) August 8, 2026

At Arsenal, they were willing to dig their heels in over the price, in the knowledge that Guimaraes really wanted the move. He had agreed personal terms with the Gunners last month and informed Newcastle of his desire to leave if a suitable offer came in.

There were also optics at play. Newcastle didn’t want to be seen as letting their talisman and a fan favourite leave without putting up a fight. Their fans would rightly have felt aggrieved.

So the negotiations dragged on, largely involving agent Kia Joorabchian. Newcastle would claim there had been no formal contact from Arsenal and felt bewildered by the process, relayed in reports of no direct contact between the clubs.

This conflict in media coverage added to the increasing frenzy attached to a potential move.

Weeks went by, before a real acceleration came last week. As Daily Mail Sport reported on Friday, July 31, a deal had been agreed in principle with a date reserved for the medical. Though a few sticking points remained.

Newly-appointed Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle also decided he wanted a final chance to try convince the Brazilian to stay put.

Guimaraes travelled to Newcastle’s La Manga training base in Spain on Monday, before waiting for permission to leave and have his medical at Arsenal after telling Jaissle of his desire to move.

The initial reports that he failed to arrive on Sunday resulted in social media sleuths tracking flights to see if Guimaraes was in the air. It had all got a bit mad.

Even the Arsenal players were braced for the move. When Riccardo Calafiori was asked about Guimaraes’ impending transfer on Wednesday night after Arsenal’s 3-1 defeat by Real Betis in Dublin, he turned to the press officer and asked: ‘Is it official yet, no?’

Berta is a tough negotiator. He loathes to overpay, which in this market is extremely hard not to do.

Arsenal had wanted to pay a smaller fee for the Brazil midfielder, who turns 29 in November, while Newcastle demanded a minimum of £80million.

That Arsenal decided to play the long game and stick to their guns frustrated some of their supporters. But the club were never in doubt of the end result.

Newly-appointed manager Matthias Jaissle made a last ditch plea to persuade him to stay

Arsenal chief Andrea Berta held his nerve on the transfer fee throughout negotiations

It’s a smart deal in a market which has, as one agent claimed, ‘gone out of control’. As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, even kids as young as 16 are being paid £20,000 a week, as in the case of Man City’s Mishel Nduka.

In the senior ranks, Chelsea bought Morgan Rogers for £117million, while Spurs splashed out £100million on Tonali.

The strategy of Arsenal and Berta has paid off - after they walked away from Rogers because their valuation of the player had been far exceeded.

The deal for Guimaraes represents value for money - and it is one Berta deserves credit for.

An Arsenal midfield, which was already dominant, now looks even more menacing. Alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard, Guimaraes completes a formidable trio.

Rice provides the ability to cover acres of space, while also being a threat going forward and strong defensively. Odegaard is in charge of creating chances in the final third.

Guimaraes, meanwhile, is an all-round No 8 who can affect games at both ends of the pitch, and brings an aggressive edge. His attempts at more ambitious passes will add some unpredictability the Gunners lack at times.

And so, after weeks of twists, denials and negotiations behind the scenes, the saga is finally over. Guimaraes is an Arsenal player – and Newcastle’s fight to keep their captain has achieved nothing more than a sizeable cheque.

Sports.title: Arsenal sign Bruno Guimaraes: Gunners complete £75m deal for Brazilian midfielder as ANOTHER Newcastle star leaves St James' Park
Sports.content:
Arsenal sign Bruno Guimaraes: Gunners complete £75m deal for Brazilian midfielder as ANOTHER Newcastle star leaves St James' Park

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Arsenal have completed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle.

The Brazilian becomes their fourth arrival of the transfer window after they made Piero Hincapie's loan permanent and signed Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier.

Guimaraes has signed a four-year deal with the option of a further 12 months.

Guimaraes said: 'I feel good, I feel amazing. I'm glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta), I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

'Well I think, after playing two World Cups, I think I'm at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I'm in the right place to do it. I'm so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I'm hopeful we can achieve our dreams.

'Big Gabi (Gabriel) was very excited. Every time he sent me the message, "We’ll wait for you, when will you come?" I'm so excited to join them, not only the Brazilians, we have an amazing squad here.

'(Declan) Rice sent me a message: "Come here and please no more fights, now we're friends". I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, in my point of view, is one of the best in Europe. Everyone is an amazing player, I'm so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well, but we have an amazing midfield.'

Arsenal have completed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United

Sporting director Andrea Berta said: 'We are delighted to welcome Bruno Guimaraes to our club.

'Bruno is a player with a great mentality and great quality, who will bring strong leadership to our squad.

'With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.

'Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.'

His arrival at the Emirates takes their summer spend to around £145m as they look to build on last season's Premier League title and Champions League final.

But the move is another complication for Newcastle, who had already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this window before Eddie Howe stepped down as manager.

Guimaraes has been an important player for the Magpies ever since joining for £40m in 2022.

But the 28-year-old told them in July that he wants to join Arsenal.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on June 25 that the Magpies were braced for an offer from the Gunners after leading agents were instructed to explore the Brazilian's options.

The World Cup star had two years remaining on his contract at St James' Park, plus the option of an extra year, hence Newcastle were able to command a strong fee.

Mikel Arteta has been keen to strengthen his central midfield options despite already having Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Fabio Vieira.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree surprise loan move for Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola looks to bolster injury-hit defence
Sports.content:
Liverpool are close to completing a loan with option to buy for Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo.

The 27-year-old is preparing to travel to link up with Liverpool on Sunday ahead of signing his contract and meeting his new team-mates. He will also undergo a medical on Sunday.

Liverpool have the option to buy Araujo for £47million.

Araujo wanted to go because after talks with coach Hansi Flick it was apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts and he believes he will find greater opportunity to do so under Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

The Spanish champions are working to offload a couple of players as they look to upgrade their squad. They are focused on signing Rodri from Manchester City and still want to strengthen their own centre-back options and at striker.

Araujo will say farewell to Barcelona team-mates on Saturday prior to heading for Merseyside on Sunday.

The Uruguay international gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at centre back and right-back.

Joe Gomez suffered a muscle injury in Liverpool's opening pre-season game, while teenage centre back Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from an ACL injury, leaving captain Virgil van Dijk as Liverpool's only fully fit senior centre back.

Liverpool have agreed a surprise deal to sign Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo on loan

The Uruguayan led Barcelona to the LaLiga title last term, but is set for a move to Anfield

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2019.

He has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona but finds himself down the pecking order in Spain, with the likes of Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin ahead of him.

Araujo has therefore taken up the opportunity to move to the Premier League, with more than two weeks still to go until Liverpool's first game of the competitive season.

The 6ft 3in central defender was at the World Cup with Uruguay and was sent off when Barcelona lost 3-0 at Stamford Bridge against Chelsea in the Champions League in November.

He didn't play a minute for his country in North America, though, as he was injured in training and didn't recover in time to feature before Marcelo Bielsa's side were knocked out in the group stage.

The Reds will face Monaco on Sunday in pre-season and then Cesc Fabregas's Como a week later, before starting their campaign against Newcastle on August 23.

Araujo will become the third major arrival at Anfield after the signings of Jacquet and winger Victor Munoz.

Liverpool remain in talks for Paris Saint-Germain pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Sports.title: Inside Erling Haaland's unlikely friendship with billionaire founder of Pretty Little Thing: Trips abroad with their WAGs, private yacht jaunts in the South of France and why they bonded
Sports.content:
A little yarn for you. Back in the day, Erling Haaland would pay visits to Pretty Little Thing's all-pink Manchester headquarters. Staff would gawp. What's he doing here?

A reasonable question. What business does a fearsome 6'4" Norse Viking have with a brand who sell trendy outfits to young women and girls?

It turns out that Haaland has a close friendship with Umar Kamani, the fashionista who founded Pretty Little Thing (PLT).

And so, Haaland being Haaland, football's chief of playful nonchalance, he would simply amble in to PLT's office for a chat with his mate. To steal one of the Norwegian's quotes: why not?

That attitude has led to a bromance blossoming. This summer, after chewing up the World Cup, Haaland has been holidaying on a yacht in the French Riviera with Kamani. It's not the first luxury trip they've been on - they have been on holidays to Monaco and St Tropez before and partied together in Dubai.

What's more, the Daily Mail can reveal that one of Kamani's close friends brokered the meeting between Haaland and Michael Jordan which recently went viral.

Erling Haaland has a surprise close friendship with Pretty Little Thing founder Umar Kamani

Haaland used to regularly stroll into PLT's Manchester office while Kamani was there

The pair have been enjoying a summer holiday in the south of France after the World Cup

It's another indicator of Haaland's rising status in the celebrity world and a well-deserved link-up after an exhausting season.

The Manchester City star, 26, recently claimed on Snapchat that his brain is 'fried' after playing in 67 games for club and country last season. Norway's first World Cup in 28 years saw them reach the quarter-finals, beating Brazil along the way. If anyone's joints need soothing in the Mediterranean sun, it's probably Haaland's.

The duo have been merrymaking at the Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc, a stunning coastal resort in Antibes where suites break the bank at up to £7,058 per night. Mind you, that's merely a drop in the ocean for Haaland, who nets close to £1million per week, and Kamani, whose net worth is estimated to be around $1billion (£797m). They've been joined by Haaland's partner Isabel Haugsend Johansen, Kamani's wife Nada, and their friends.

Kamani sat with Haaland's family for Norway's World Cup last-16 victory over Brazil - in which the striker scored two - and the pair linked up for their jaunt almost immediately after they were knocked out by England.

Their friendship dates back to 2022, right when Haaland signed for Manchester City in a £51m deal from Borussia Dortmund. It was a proud moment for the young striker - his father, Alf-Inge, had played for the club, and Erling, who was born in Leeds, claimed to have been a fan his whole life.

Umar, himself a City supporter, was close to some of the players, and they introduced the pair. A source explains that they simply hit it off and the pair have got on ever since. Their shared passion for football, luxury watches, and adventure helps.

By the winter of 2022, five months after they met, Haaland was close enough with Kamani that he received an invitation to the couturier's mansion in Dubai.

That was during the Qatar World Cup, a tournament Haaland missed out on as Norway failed to qualify. The Manchester City star took a mid-season break and visited Kamani with sports therapist Mario Pafundi, who remains one of Haaland's closest allies to this day.

Haaland's viral link-up with Michael Jordan was brokered by one of Kamani's close friends

Kamani's wife, Nada, and Haaland's partner Isabel Haugsend Johansen have also joined them on their trip (pictured in 2024)

In the summer of 2023, Haaland and his father joined Kamani on a luxury superyacht with a host of big names. Among them was Tommy Hilfiger - yes, the man behind the eponymous brand. On the same trip, the striker met up with Prince Albert II of Monaco for lunch. As you do.

To welcome in 2024, Haaland and his girlfriend attended an exclusive party hosted by Kamani in Dubai. The likes of Anthony Joshua and Derek Chisora were there. Fortunately no fights broke out. Kamani turned up in a pink suit and a wore a gigantic mascot head, seemingly of himself.

Haaland also visited the Kamani Club, a private gym owned by the businessman in Dubai. They hung out together in side-by-side ice baths, smiling for a photo, and trained with athletes from a range of disciplines including boxing and tennis.

As far as we are aware, Haaland was not at Kamani's £20m, four-day wedding to his wife Nada in 2024. The lovebirds tied the knot across two lavish ceremonies in the south of France after a fairytale proposal involving a £1.45m ring in August 2021.

But in many ways it makes sense that Haaland and Kamani would become friends, because they share similarities. Haaland is a workhorse powered by long hours in the gym, gigantic barbecued steaks, raw milk, and raw honey. A man who endures the ice bath five times a week. No method is too maverick, no sacrifice too large to prevent him from reaching his goal.

That level of industry is shared by Kamani. The 38-year-old's career has taken him global, but at heart he is a Manchester lad.

He grew up in a house of 18 family members in Chorlton, southwest of the city centre. His grandfather, Abdullah, had escaped war-riddled Kenya in the 1960s and made a living selling handbags from a market stall once he had reached the north west.

Kamani was always destined to go into fashion. His father, Mahmud, co-founded Boohoo in 2006 with Carol Kane. Young Umar caught the bug and set up PLT with his brother Adam in 2012.

After a season of 67 games, Haaland has been letting his hair down in the French Riviera

Haaland and Kamani are pictured with fashionista Tommy Hilfiger during a yacht party

'It’s impossible for me not to be working in fashion. I was born into fashion. That’s like saying if you couldn’t breathe what would you do?' he once told Drapers.

Pretty Little Thing revolutionised the fashion retail industry - suddenly, young people could buy dirt-cheap outfits that looked similar to what their favourite celebrities were wearing.

Design teams monitored the social media feeds of celebs, and within days the company could have rolled out a low-cost mimic of the outfit for regular consumers. Clothes went for as little as six pence.

Not everything was sunshine and roses though. The brand was accused of fuelling a throwaway culture - which is bad for the environment - and killing the high street with deals promising 99 per cent reductions.

On a darker note, its parent company, Boohoo, the Kamani family business, was accused in 2020 of paying employees as little as £3.50 an hour and forcing staff to continue working in shoddy conditions, even after some tested positive for coronavirus.

At a factory in Leicester, the 'sweatshop' scandal resulted in National Crime Agency investigation. The revelations caused a crash in the company's share price. Kamani left PLT as CEO in 2023 but returned to the company in September 2024.

Earlier this year, Boohoo, in which Kamani owns a minority stake, was hit with £10m worth of new legal claims from investors who accuse his father, Mahmud, of knowing about the 'sweatshop' conditions which led to the share price collapse of 42 per cent. Mahmud said in 2020 that he 'cannot possibly know everything in this business'.

Whatever the outcome, one thing is for certain: Umar Kamani and Haaland's bromance helps them let their hair down a few times a year alongside their stressful jobs, and gets them opportunities and access they once would have thought unthinkable.

Sports.title: Revealed: 'Three strict measures' Jose Mourinho has imposed at Real Madrid to lay down his authority - after legendary boss was hired to improve discipline at the Bernabeu
Sports.content:
Revealed: 'Three strict measures' Jose Mourinho has imposed at Real Madrid to lay down his authority - after legendary boss was hired to improve discipline at the Bernabeu

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jose Mourinho has wasted little time putting his stamp on Real Madrid after introducing three strict new measures at the Bernabeu, according to reports.

The legendary former Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham manager returned to the Spanish giants this summer to help improve discipline and restore order to the dressing room after Real Madrid endured a disappointing season without a trophy.

Tasked with managing the personalities of Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior, who agreed a new six-year deal at the club this week, Mourinho has reportedly focused on three key areas to improve standards at the Bernabeu.

According to Spanish outlet AS, the Portuguese has implemented new measures over nutrition, punctuality and recovery from injury.

Firstly, players are told exactly what to eat every day by the club's nutritionist, who used to hold an advisory role but now sets menus for all meals, including breakfast and even afternoon snacks.

Before he arrived, there was more freedom over diet and nutrition but Mourinho is determined to have the kitchen structured around performance as opposed to each player's personal preference.

Jose Mourinho has reportedly introduced three strict new measures at Real Madrid

Rules around nutrition, punctuality and injury recovery has changed since his arrival

For now, despite losing their freedom over food, the players have reacted positively to the new measure, according to the newspaper.

Meanwhile, Mourinho has also changed how players will be punished if they turn up late to training or a meeting at Valdebebas.

Before, poor punctuality would result in financial fines, but now players who turn up late are required to train away from the rest of the team, working out alone in the gym.

Mourinho insists on his players arriving one hour before the start of training and has urged that anyone failing to adhere to this rule will be sanctioned, regardless of status, role or hierarchy.

Finally, the Portuguese boss has ordered that all injury recovery sessions and programmes must now exclusively take place at Real Madrid's Valdebebas training complex.

Eager to make rehabilitation more of a collective task rather than an individual one, Mourinho has banned external treatments and urged that every single medical detail must be coordinated through the club and his staff.

Real Madrid, who finished 12 points behind archrivals Barcelona in LaLiga's title race last season, begin the new campaign with a trip to Espanyol on August 22.

Sports.title: Matheus Nunes opens up on Pep Guardiola's emotional Man City exit, adapting to his new role as a right back - and 'p***ing off' John Stones!
Sports.content:
Matheus Nunes opens up on Pep Guardiola's emotional Man City exit, adapting to his new role as a right back - and 'p***ing off' John Stones!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Eighteen hours after a needlessly dramatic last-minute win over Leeds last November, John Stones ambled out at Manchester City's training complex with Matheus Nunes firmly in his sights.

What might appear an unlikely friendship was forged in wanting to make others laugh. Nunes started most of his days by attempting to get under the skin of Stones at breakfast. Or, in his own words, 'p*** John off'.

So when the Portuguese had been severely at fault for a Dominic Calvert-Lewin goal that launched an improbable comeback, rectifying one mistake from full back only to then lose possession inside his own box in dizzying fashion, Stones saw his opportunity to exact some revenge.

Sources say in that warm down session, the centre half mercilessly mocked his great mate for a comical part in the goal. Nunes had to just take it.

Stones felt safe doing that for two reasons: City won the game via Phil Foden in stoppage time and, more importantly, Nunes had felt a sense of belonging at right back for some time prior.

He had not been able to accept being shifted there by Pep Guardiola for six long months in 2025. He could have left the club.

Matheus Nunes has transitioned from a midfielder to a right back at Manchester City

But once the Leeds gaffe came around, the 27-year-old was already comfortable in his new skin – any mental fragility gone - and now he heads into this Premier League as Enzo Maresca's first choice. This comes after those closest to him had to cajole him into believing in a reimagined destiny while at his lowest ebb.

'When I was playing as a winger, Bernardo [Silva] would call me Thierry Henry,' Nunes says. 'Then I played as a full back and he called me Cafu.

'Bernardo and Ruben [Dias] were so annoying all the time, they were in my head constantly: 'You were good there, you were good there. You need to accept it.' And I was like, no, no, no, all the time.

'I always told my friends that I wasn't a full back. At a certain point you just have to see what the people are saying. You can't be denying it for the rest of your life. If you do, maybe you miss your chance. Now I feel like a full back.'

Nunes struggled to countenance the switch from central midfield, where he had excelled at Wolves. During the process of shifting him into defence Pep Guardiola once said that Nunes wasn't 'clever enough' to feature in the middle for City – comments he privately clarified with the player a day later.

The integration was not easy, Nunes in and out, bruised by mistakes during a derby defeat too – one of them glaring, under-hitting a back pass and then barging Amad over to concede a penalty in blind panic.

'Individually I would say this is probably the most difficult game,' he adds. 'In my head after the game… when you do mistakes as a midfielder, you would never affect the game like that one. I did one mistake and it led to a goal, and then you end up losing the game and that's all you think in your head, you know?

'But it was not only that, it was me coming from a place where it was uncomfortable for me, a position where it was uncomfortable for me, not being able to accept it, because I wasn't accepting it. In my head, it was 'I'm not a full-back. I'm not a full-back'. That's all I was thinking about.

'I think in the Club World Cup, my mindset started to change. Oh, I can actually play good. I had maybe three or four games in a row and then the beginning of last season I started playing every single game. Then your head just flips and you can see it through.'

Nunes saw a psychologist during that transition and Guardiola ended up revealing that he observed elite potential in him as a defender. 'If I didn't change my mindset I would never have played good there and he would never have said stuff like that. He probably said that because he started to see what others couldn't see.

'Then actually seeing Pep during training, the way he believed in me, I felt there was a bit of a difference in the way that we interacted with each other. This stuff, you just feel it, it's not something that I can explain. And once you start seeing all of this stuff, it changes the mindset. It was not easy, of course, but I had a decision to make: do I want to play or do I not want to play? And I wanted to play.'

Nunes begins to become emotional when Guardiola's exit is raised. He talks about the video montage shown to players and staff - of Guardiola's speeches and moments with the squad across a decade - when the manager officially announced his departure to the room.

Nunes offered a new insight into Guardiola's departure and said it was still difficult to talk about

Join the discussion Did Pep Guardiola’s position changes for players help City reach new heights or hold back their talents?

'A lot of people were crying,' Nunes says. 'Pep held it together. He just wanted to get it over [quickly]. It became real that he was actually leaving. It's difficult to talk about.

'It's very hard to say goodbye to someone who gave so much to us all. Someone who put the club to a level that seems unreachable again. What he did was unbelievable. A lot of things are going to change. I've never been in the club without him. It's never easy to say goodbye.'

Adding Silva and Stones into that equation has made it a sombre summer for Nunes specifically.

'Huge losses,' he says. 'If you look at it, John was a very important figure in the club. He was always a joker. The three of us were. I'm just being myself, and then I end up being a clown sometimes. What's the point of life if you're not having a laugh?'

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's 'alleged mistress received six-figure pay-off from UEFA following affair while he was in senior position' - as FIFA president faces mounting calls to quit
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's 'alleged mistress received six-figure pay-off from UEFA following affair while he was in senior position' - as FIFA president faces mounting calls to quit

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The pressure on Gianni Infantino to resign as FIFA president has grown after it emerged UEFA paid off his alleged mistress during his time with the European governing body.

The Telegraph reported the woman received a six-figure sum following an alleged affair with Infantino when he was UEFA general secretary.

It is claimed the junior employee was promoted by Infantino and given a 30 per cent pay rise at the time of their relationship. UEFA's then president, Michel Platini, was reportedly aware and raised concerns with Infantino.

The organisation decided she would depart her role with a substantial sum, paid for by UEFA, which also covered the costs for her to do an MBA course at a business school worth £45,000 per year.

UEFA confirmed the payment and its awareness of the relationship between Infantino and the woman in a statement to The Telegraph.

Infantino has been married to Leena Al Ashqar since 2001 and the couple have four daughters.

UEFA paid off a female employee who had an alleged affair with Gianni Infantino during his time at the organisation

Infantino is under pressure to quit following his failed FIFA Forward Enterprise scheme

'We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school,' UEFA said. 'The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.

'Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all UEFA employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.'

The Telegraph also reported there had been complaints about Infantino's behaviour at FIFA, claims strenuously denied by football's worldwide governing body.

Infantino became UEFA secretary general – a position second only to the presidency in terms of power – in 2009. He started in 2000 as a lawyer before working his way up in the organisation.

The now 56-year-old was elected FIFA president in 2016 following the downfall of Sepp Blatter. He was re-elected in 2019 and 2023, and had been expected to secure a fourth term in March.

The revelations cast further doubt on Infantino's position at FIFA with the Swiss-Italian facing widespread calls to quit after he was forced to abandon a widely condemned plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

UEFA are leading the charge to dethrone Infantino as FIFA president in response to the scrapped proposal, pledging to boycott any FIFA tournaments so long as he remains in the role.

But he appears to retain support from Africa, South America and Asia – which is enough to fend off any leadership challenge ahead of the election, scheduled to take place at the FIFA congress in Morocco in March.

Mexico this week broke ranks from CONCACAF's opposition to Infantino, reaffirming their confidence in the FIFA leadership.

UEFA's current refusal to play in FIFA competitions will cause the governing body significant commercial problems, potentially prompting Infantino to reconsider his position at the top of world football.

But the FIFA president has shown no sign of relenting thus far after being supported by the governing body's hierarchy following crisis talks on Wednesday, vowing to fight on despite demands he resign.

Infantino is facing a possible investigation after Norwegian FA president Lise Klaveness said she would report him to FIFA's Ethics Committee.

The complaint will not only challenge the proposed sale of a £3.1billion stake in the World Cup to private investors, but also the decision to award an ad hoc FIFA Peace Prize to President Donald Trump and the suspension of Folarin Balogun's red card at the World Cup following alleged political pressure from Trump.

Sports.title: BREAKING: Arsenal announce £75m Bruno Guimaraes deal as next two transfers become clear
Sports.content:
BREAKING: Arsenal announce £75m Bruno Guimaraes deal as next two transfers become clear

After nearly two months of chasing him in what became a transfer saga, Arsenal have finally wrapped up the signing of Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes for a cool £75million

View Image Bruno Guimaraes has left Newcastle to join Arsenal (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes has been announced as Arsenal's latest signing, penning a five-year deal with the Gunners. The Newcastle captain joins in a £75million deal, with Mikel Arteta now set to go after a new winger and a centre-back.

‌



After several weeks of negotiations, Arsenal agreed a deal with the Magpies earlier this week to secure the Brazilian's signature. Not long after, the 28-year-old left Newcastle's training camp in La Manga, Spain to fly to North London and rubber-stamp the deal.

‌



Guimaraes has officially become the Gunners' second most expensive signing of all time, with only Declan Rice's £105m move from West Ham ahead of him. He'll wear his favourite No.39 shirt at the Emirates.

‌



Speaking after completing his move, Guimaraes vowed to be a 'warrior' for Arsenal, who he joined to win trophies.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gabriel Jesus' agent addresses Arsenal transfer exit after being spotted at rival club READ MORE :

FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21 READ MORE :

The midfielder is the fourth confirmed signing this summer, following deals for Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis. Arsenal won't be stopping there, though, with Arteta set to turn his attention to signing the wide forward area and cover at the back for William Saliba.

‌



Vinicius Junior had been their top target, but Arteta and Co. will have to look elsewhere now that the Brazilian has signed a contract extension at Real Madrid. Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola is a known target but also has interest from Liverpool.

Meanwhile, Ezri Konsa is wanted by Arsenal in their search for a defender. The Gunners have already had a £40m bid for the England international rejected by Aston Villa, but they're reportedly preparing a second offer closer to his £60m asking price.

Have Arsenal got a bargain with Bruno Guimaraes? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



Addressing his departure from St James' Park, Guimaraes said: "This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together. I fell in love with this place. I really mean that.

"From my first day, the supporters, my team-mates, Eddie (Howe) and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home. I thank PIF, our chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club.

"I also want to say thank you to David (Hopkinson) and Ross (Wilson) for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.

‌



"This move is very tough because Newcastle means so much to me, but I wanted to experience something new in my life. I feel ready for a new challenge for myself and my family.

"I had a very positive conversation with Matthias Jaissle, and I leave knowing the club is in very good hands. To the supporters, thank you will never be enough, but I say it with all my heart. I will always be proud to have been part of this club's journey. Thank you for everything."

Sports.title: Stevenage 'set standard' as Alex Revell lauds Carabao Cup victory over Wycombe
Sports.content:
Stevenage 'set standard' as Alex Revell lauds Carabao Cup victory over Wycombe

Stevenage progressed to the second round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2016 with Friday's 2-1 victory over Wycombe at Adams Park, leaving manager Alex Revell full of praise for his side

View 2 Images Stevenage manager Alex Revell was pleased with his side's performance in Friday's Carabao Cup defeat of Wycombe

Stevenage manager Alex Revell said Friday's Carabao Cup victory over Wycombe is "the standard" for his side this season as they progressed to the second round for the first time since 2016.

‌



The Boro secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over their hosts at Adams Park thanks to a 95th-minute winner from summer signing Josh Magennis, ensuring they would get their 2026-27 campaign off to the perfect start as they look to build on last season's play-off finish in League One.

‌



On the same night, Wolves defeated League Two outfit Port Vale 3-0 and Middlesbrough beat Wrexham 1-0 in an all-Championship affair, while a further 29 Carabao Cup first-round fixtures are set to take place today.

‌



Carabao Cup first round TV guide: How to watch every match live this weekend READ MORE :

Stevenage, who finished five places and 12 points ahead of Wycombe (11th) in the third tier last season, were certainly made to work for their victory, however, as the Chairboys responded well to going behind in the 27th minute.

Both sides could have arguably put the game to bed during the first half, and it looked as though the tie would be heading to a penalty shootout following a relatively lackluster second half, but veteran forward Magennis popped up in the dying seconds to steal the win for his new side.

Following the game, Revell said he was "really pleased" with Stevenage's overall performance, having demanded a certain standard from his players heading into the new campaign.

‌



"For us, we wanted to set a standard, and we have certain demands to maintain what we achieved last year and try to be better," Revell told The Mirror. "There's no better feeling than winning. For us, it was a really good challenge and really nice to start the season with a win."

What made things even better for Revell, a former Stevenage player himself, is that the winner came from not just one of his new signings, but one of his substitutions, as Magennis came off the bench to head home the winner.

"You look a genius, don't you?" he laughed. "Really pleased for Josh, he's worked really hard. When you get good delivery and timing, and somebody wants to score a goal, it’s a great ending to the game for us.

‌



"We just have to get our head down and keep doing what we've been doing throughout pre-season, working as hard as we can to keep improving. Tonight, there were signs of that as well, and we'll look to keep that winning mentality going."

View 2 Images Wycombe manager Michael Duff was left rueing his side's missed opportunities to win the game

As for Wycombe, they will look to quickly bounce back with a victory in their opening League One game of the season away to Blackpool next week, though manager Michael Duff couldn't help but rue the missed opportunity for his side on home soil.

Article continues below

"The players said it themselves at halftime, we need to be better in both boxes," Duff told The Mirror. "We missed a load of chances and given them a really, really cheap goal.

"Ultimately, they didn't execute what we wanted in terms of being better in both boxes; that's why we've ended up losing the game."

Sports.title: Four left-backs Man Utd can sign after Newcastle block Lewis Hall transfer move
Sports.content:
Four left-backs Man Utd can sign after Newcastle block Lewis Hall transfer move

Manchester United have been forced to turn to other targets in their attempts to sign a left-back this summer after Newcastle made it clear that Lewis Hall isn't for sale

View 5 Images Lewis Hall won't be joining Manchester United it seems (Image: (Photo by Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

Manchester United have made little ground in their efforts to sign a left-back this summer, with top target Lewis Hall appearing to be out of reach.

‌



Newcastle have made it clear to United that after selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, they are in no mood to offload Hall, too. It would take a bid way beyond United's means to test that stance meaning that, with 24 days of the transfer window left, United must look elsewhere.

‌



Michael Carrick is keen to add competition for places at left-back, where Luke Shaw remains the first choice. Harry Amass has featured in pre-season but could be sold or loaned out, while Noussair Mazraoui and Diego Dalot are more comfortable on the right side of defence, and Patrick Dorgu has shone further forward under Carrick's management.

‌



United have already landed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos to address their most pressing need in central midfield but could find left-back a more difficult prospect. Here, Mirror Football takes a look at the other contenders.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry READ MORE :

Antonee Robinson

Robinson had been a regular name in transfer reports, but fell off the radar somewhat last season due to a dip in form. But his 2024-25 campaign, in which he returned 10 assists in the Premier League, hasn't faded from the memory of scouts and sporting directors yet.

‌



The 28-year-old, who played for the United States at the World Cup in the summer, has eye-catching pace and loves to go forward - something that sets him apart from the more conservative (and much slower) Shaw. He has two years left on his Fulham contract, so could be affordable.

View 5 Images Antonee Robinson is an option for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

El Hadji Malick Diouf

Diouf was relegated with West Ham last season and is far from the finished article, but at 21 years old could be a player for the future. He contributed five assists in 32 Premier League matches for the Hammers last season and is a regular for Senegal.

‌



West Ham don't want to sell and, having shipped out Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville for big fees already, are under little pressure to do so. Signed from Slavia Prague for £19million last summer, he still has four years left on his contract and West Ham have already rejected one bid from Brentford for his services, with a second offer expected.

View 5 Images El Hadji Malick Diouf had a good first season at West Ham (Image: Julian Finney)

Jorge Salinas

Another one for the future, rather than a serious contender for Shaw's place in the starting XI. The 19-year-old Racing Santander player is reportedly on United's radar.

‌



He is highly rated and has a €16m (£13.7m) release clause, making him very affordable. However, United could face competition from Barcelona, who often hoover up the best talent in Spain and are looking for a replacement for Joao Cancelo, who is set to make the move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.

View 5 Images Jorge Salinas is on Manchester United's radar

David Raum

The RB Leipzig captain is an energetic, durable and experienced player who is capable of displacing Shaw from the United team. He is much more mobile than Show, who is about to start his 13th season with the Red Devils.

‌



Raum has a strong left foot, is not shy of crossing, and could link up nicely with Benjamin Sesko, who is a real aerial threat and knows the German from his time at Leipzig. The 28-year-old is settled at Leipzig, who have just sold Yan Diomande to Real Madrid for £120m, so are in no rush to cash in.

However, the Germany international recently revealed he is yet to hold talks about extending his contract, which has less than a year left to run. "It's up to the club to decide when they approach me, what they offer, how much appreciation they show, what their plans are for me, and where they want to go in the coming years," he said.

View 5 Images David Raum has entered the final year of his RB Leipzig contract (Image: Ralf Ibing - firo sportphoto/Getty Images)

‌



"Of course, I have to listen to that and make my own decision. I'm 28 now, and naturally I also have dreams and goals. You always have to see how that fits together with the club's plans, ideas and objectives for the next few years."

He added: "The club generally doesn't like to let a player run down his contract. I don't know what they have planned with me. At the moment, it doesn't look like they want to sell me or get rid of me. I feel a lot of appreciation here."

Depending on your interpretation, that is either a player trying to force the club to the negotiating table for a new deal, or a player issuing a come-get-me plea.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
